source.title: Limb apraxia and the "affordance competition hypothesis"

confidence_rationale: The chip asked whether ideomotor apraxia -- classically 'intention without correct movement' -- has been read as a representational (direction) deficit. This review answers no from the other direction: it reframes apraxic errors within Cisek's affordance competition hypothesis as 'an abnormal sensitivity to competition when multiple affordances are present and/or a poor ability to exert cognitive control over this competition'. The locus is the SELECTION competition and its control, not the goal representation. Recorded as a Q2 null with unknown direction: it neither supports nor weakens MECH-535, it documents that the intention-without-direction disorders adjacent to catatonia have been placed on the gating/competition axis.
failure_signatures: Apraxic errors are attributed to heightened affordance competition or weak control over it -- a selection/control locus; the review does not consider a degraded goal or direction representation as a cause.
The ideomotor/ideational split is mapped onto the dorsal/ventral stream (implementation vs concept), which is a coarser division than proximity vs direction within one representation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Limb apraxia has been classified into ideational (deficit in the concept of a movement, ventral stream) and ideomotor (deficit in accurate implementation, dorsal stream). The authors argue that 'at least some aspects of apraxia may reflect an abnormal sensitivity to competition when multiple affordances are present ... and/or a poor ability to exert cognitive control over this competition', placing apraxia within Cisek's (2007) affordance competition hypothesis.
mapping.ree_translation: In REE terms this puts apraxia on the selection/gating axis (competition among candidate actions and top-down control of it -- MECH-202's territory), not on the representational axis MECH-535 occupies. It is the neuropsychological counterpart to the catatonia literature's placement of its own deficit in top-down modulation. Q2's null therefore extends across the adjacent 'intention without correct movement' disorders: the field's explanatory habit is to reach for competition and control before it reaches for a degraded goal representation.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A framing paper, not a test; it proposes a reading of apraxia and reviews compatible evidence. It says nothing about oscillation or about proximity vs direction, so the null is again one of omission. Apraxia concerns object use and gesture, far from a foraging gridworld.
mapping.source_context: Human neuropsychology; limb apraxia after left-hemisphere stroke; conceptual review.

confidence_components.notes: Well-argued conceptual review in a mid-tier venue; its contribution to this pull is taxonomic (where the adjacent syndromes are placed), which is why mapping fidelity to MECH-535's mechanism is low.
